claim: Transcription factors operate by the combined activity of their DNA-binding domains (DBDs) and effector domains (EDs) enabling the coordination of gene expression on a genomic scale.
source: Transcription factors (TFs) operate by the combined activity of their DNA-binding domains (DBDs) and effector domains (EDs) enabling the coordination of gene expression on a genomic scale.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about transcription factor structure and function.

claim: In vivo delivery of an engineered DNA-binding protein uncoupled from the repressor domain can produce efficient and gene-specific transcriptional silencing.
source: Here we show that in vivo delivery of an engineered DNA-binding protein uncoupled from the repressor domain can produce efficient and gene-specific transcriptional silencing.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: ZF6-DB targets 20 base pairs (bp) of a RHO cis-regulatory element (CRE).
source: To interfere with RHODOPSIN (RHO) gain-of-function mutations we engineered the ZF6-DNA-binding protein (ZF6-DB) that targets 20 base pairs (bp) of a RHOcis-regulatory element (CRE)
evidence: This is a design specification of the engineered protein, confirmed by experimental data.

claim: AAV vector-mediated expression of ZF6-DB in photoreceptors demonstrates Rho specific transcriptional silencing.
source: demonstrate Rho specific transcriptional silencing upon adeno-associated viral (AAV) vector-mediated expression in photoreceptors.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data including qPCR, immunofluorescence, and RNA-seq results.

claim: The 20 bp-long genomic DNA sequence is necessary for RHO expression.
source: The data show that the 20 bp-long genomic DNA sequence is necessary for RHO expression
evidence: This is supported by deletion experiments showing loss of eGFP expression when the ZF6-cis sequence is deleted.

claim: Photoreceptor delivery of ZF6-DB blocks Rho expression with negligible genome-wide transcript perturbations.
source: photoreceptor delivery of the corresponding cognate synthetic trans-acting factor ZF6-DB without the intrinsic transcriptional repression properties of the canonical ED blocks Rho expression with negligible genome-wide transcript perturbations.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing only 19 DEGs with ZF6-DB treatment.

claim: In eukaryotes TF DNA binding and effector activities are typically structurally modular.
source: However, in eukaryotes TF DNA binding and effector activities are typically structurally modular (Brent, 1985)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: TF DNA-binding domain controls the TF topology on genomic targets.
source: consisting of a DNA-binding domain (DBD) controlling the TF topology on genomic targets
evidence: This is established knowledge about transcription factor function, supported by citation.

claim: Effector domains recruit co-activator or co-repressor complexes.
source: an effector domain (ED) (Brent, 1985; Kadonaga, 2004) that recruits co-activator or co-repressor complexes (Malik and Roeder, 2010; Perissi et al., 2010)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Effector domain recruitment of co-activator or co-repressor complexes results in either transcriptional activation or repression of gene regulatory networks.
source: that recruits co-activator or co-repressor complexes (Malik and Roeder, 2010; Perissi et al., 2010) resulting in either transcriptional activation or repression of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) (Neph et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Engineered TFs mimic the design of natural TFs.
source: Engineered TFs mimic the design of natural TFs (Pavletich and Pabo, 1991; Beerli and Barbas, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The DBD module is engineered to recognize unique genome sites to generate target specificity.
source: To generate target specificity the DBD module is engineered to recognize unique genome sites (Beerli and Barbas, 2002)
evidence: This is established knowledge about engineered TF design, supported by citation.

claim: Transcriptional activation or repressor properties are conferred by the selection of the ED.
source: whereas the transcriptional activation or repressor properties are conferred by the selection of the ED (Konermann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Engineered DNA-binding proteins without canonical ED activity possess transcriptional repression properties.
source: here we investigated the hypothesis that engineered DNA-binding proteins without canonical ED activity possess transcriptional repression properties.
evidence: This is the hypothesis being tested in the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: RHO gain-of-function mutations are those most commonly associated with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP).
source: As a transcriptional repression target we selected the G-protein-coupled Receptor Rhodopsin (RHO) gene whose gain-of-function mutations are those most commonly associated with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP), an incurable form of blindness (Dryja et al., 1990).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa is an incurable form of blindness.
source: autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP), an incurable form of blindness (Dryja et al., 1990).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: ZF6-DB was generated by deconstructing an engineered TF composed of a DBD and the KRAB repressor domain.
source: We generated a DNA-binding protein targeted to a cis-regulatory element (CRE) of the human proximal RHO promoter region by deconstructing an engineered TF (synthetic) composed of a DBD (ZF6-DNA-binding protein, ZF6-DB) and the ED (Kruppel-associated box, KRAB repressor domain, KRAB)
evidence: This describes the experimental design and construction of the ZF6-DB protein.

claim: ZF6-KRAB is effective in repressing specifically the human RHO transgene carried in an adRP mouse model.
source: which we have shown to be effective in repressing specifically the human RHO transgene carried in an adRP mouse model (Mussolino et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: ZF6-cis is found at -84 bp to -65 bp from the transcription start site (TSS) of the human RHO gene.
source: The deletion of the ED resulted in a protein, ZF6-DB targeting 20 base pairs of genomic CRE, here named ZF6-cis, found at -84 bp to -65 bp from the transcription start site (TSS) of the human RHO gene (Figure 1a; Mitton et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Genomic ZF6-cis is without apparent photoreceptor-specific endogenous transcription factor-binding sites.
source: Genomic ZF6-cis is without apparent photoreceptor-specific endogenous transcription factor-binding sites (TFBS; Figure 1a), as reported (Kwasnieski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: AAV-RHO-cis-del-EGFP showed loss of eGFP expression compared to the control vector AAV-RHO-EGFP after delivery to porcine retinal photoreceptor.
source: The 776 bp-long RHO promoter fragment carrying the ZF6-cis deletion upstream of the eGFP reporter gene (AAV-RHO-cis-del-EGFP), after delivery to the porcine retinal photoreceptor, showed loss of eGFP expression compared to the control vector (AAV-RHO-EGFP) (Figure 1b,c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b,c.

claim: ZF6-cis CRE is necessary for RHO expression (at least for the 776 bp region used in the assay).
source: This suggests that ZF6-cis CRE is necessary for RHO expression (at least for the 776 bp region used in the assay)
evidence: This is inferred from the deletion experiment results.

claim: Binding of the synthetic ZF6-DB trans-acting counterpart of ZF6-cis may repress RHO transcription.
source: and that binding of the synthetic ZF6-DB trans-acting counterpart of ZF6-cis, may indeed repress RHO transcription.
evidence: This is a hypothesis inferred from the deletion experiment results.

claim: ChIP experiments showed occupancy of the ZF6-cis target genomic sequence by the DNA-binding protein ZF6-DB.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) experiments to evaluate binding to the ZF6-cis target genomic sequence showed occupancy by the DNA-binding protein ZF6-DB (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The porcine retina shares 19 out of 20 DNA bp with the human genomic ZF6-cis sequence.
source: To evaluate whether ZF6-DB represses transcription of the RHO gene in a physiological genomic context, we used the porcine retina (Mussolino et al., 2011b), which shares 19 out of 20 DNA bp with the human genomic ZF6-cis sequence (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a and citation.

claim: Subretinal delivery of AAV8-CMV-ZF6-DB at 1x10^10 gc resulted in a 45% decrease of porcine Rho transcript levels at 15 days post-injection.
source: Subretinal delivery of a low AAV8 vector dose (1x1010 genome copies; gc) of ZF6-DB (AAV8-CMV-ZF6-DB) resulted in a 45% decrease of porcine Rho transcript levels at 15 days post-injection (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Immunofluorescence analysis showed depletion of Rho protein and consequent collapse of the rod outer segments in ZF6-DB positive cells.
source: Immunofluorescence analysis showed depletion of Rho protein and consequent collapse of the rod outer segments in ZF6-DB positive cells (Figure 1e,f).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1e,f.

claim: Despite the lack of detectable Rho expression in most of the transduced rods, rows of photoreceptor nuclei were preserved from degeneration at 15 days post-injection.
source: Despite the lack of detectable Rho expression in most of the transduced rods, rows of photoreceptor nuclei were preserved from degeneration at this time point (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: FACS analysis on eGFP-labelled rod cells showed virtually a 'somatic knock-out' of Rho expression (~85% decrease of Rho transcript levels) in retina co-transduced with eGFP and ZF6-DB vector.
source: Fifteen days after injection, the retina were disaggregated and FACS-sorted. The retina co-transduced with eGFP and ZF6-DB vector showed virtually a 'somatic knock-out' of Rho expression (~85% decrease of Rho transcript levels; Figure 1g,h).
evidence: This is supported by FACS and qPCR data shown in Figure 1g,h.

claim: Low vector doses of ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB (1x10^10 gc) resulted in about twenty-fold lower expression levels compared to Crx and Nrl.
source: The low vector doses delivered to the porcine retina (1x1010 gc) resulted in about twenty-fold lower expression levels of the ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB transgenes compared to Crx and Nrl, two retina-specific TFs (Swaroop et al., 2010) (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq expression data shown in Figure 2a and citation.

claim: Despite low expression levels, robust Rho transcriptional repression was observed.
source: Of note, despite these low expression levels, we observed robust Rho transcriptional repression (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: ZF6-DB protein generated about ten-fold less transcriptional perturbation compared with the ZF6-KRAB protein (19 vs. 222 DEGs).
source: Remarkably, in vivo the ZF6-DB protein generated about ten-fold less transcriptional perturbation compared with the ZF6-KRAB protein (19 vs. 222 DEGs; Figure 2e).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The magnitude of perturbation by ZF6-DB is twenty five-fold lower than that induced by the ablation of an endogenous rod-specific TF NRL (500 DEGs vs 19 DEGs).
source: Notably, this magnitude of perturbation is twenty five-fold lower than that induced by the ablation of an endogenous rod-specific TF (NRL, 500 DEGs vs 19 DEGs, ZF6-DBD; [Roger et al., 2014]).
evidence: This is a comparison to published data, supported by citation.

claim: ZF6-DB–induced down-regulation is restricted to the Rho biochemical interactor Gnat1.
source: Retinal-specific pathway analysis of DEGs showed that ZF6-DB–induced down-regulation is restricted to the Rho biochemical interactor Gnat1 (Palczewski, 2012)
evidence: This is supported by pathway analysis of RNA-seq data and citation.

claim: ZF6-DB induced up-regulation of 2 genes associated with acute phase inflammatory response, alpha-2-macroglobulin (A2m) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (Gfap).
source: and the up-regulation of 2 genes associated with acute phase inflammatory response, alpha-2-macroglobulin (A2m) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (Gfap) (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by pathway analysis shown in Figure 2c.

claim: ZF6-KRAB induced the de-regulation of 17 retinal network associated genes.
source: ZF6-KRAB induced the de-regulation of 17 retinal network associated genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by pathway analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both ZF6-DB and the consequent Rho down-regulation marginally interferes with photoreceptor specific pathways, apart from Gnat1 repression.
source: These results suggest that both ZF6-DB and the consequent Rho down-regulation marginally interferes with photoreceptor specific pathways, apart from Gnat1 repression
evidence: This is inferred from the RNA-seq pathway analysis results.

claim: The up-regulation of the inflammatory response genes may be due to the collapse of the retinal scaffold caused by Rho depletion.
source: and that the up-regulation of the inflammatory response genes may be due to the collapse of the retinal scaffold caused by Rho depletion.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed inflammatory gene up-regulation.

claim: Both ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB drive similar perturbation in the expression of 16 genes, which represent 84% of the entire pool of ZF6-DB DEGs.
source: The intersection of retinal transcriptome changes between ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB showed that both drive similar perturbation in the expression of 16 genes, which represent 84% of the entire pool of ZF6-DB DEGs (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Both ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB generated similar functional effects, i.e. concordant up- or down- differential expression of the 16 shared genes.
source: Consistently, both ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB generated similar functional effects, i.e. concordant up- or down- differential expression of these 16 shared genes (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Both ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB bind to similar genomic targets.
source: These results suggest that both ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB bind to similar genomic targets.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar transcriptional effects observed.

claim: Both ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB proteins bind the ZF6-cis RHO DNA target site with similar affinities.
source: We next studied whether the differential transcriptional repression induced by ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB was due to similar biochemical binding properties for the ZF6-cis DNA target. Both ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB proteins bind the ZF6-cis RHO DNA target site with similar affinities (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by gel mobility shift assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Despite the presence of an active canonical repressor domain, ZF6-KRAB generated Rho silencing by DNA binding.
source: These data suggest that, despite the presence of an active canonical repressor domain, ZF6-KRAB generated Rho silencing by DNA binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar binding affinities and silencing effects of ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB.

claim: ZF6-DB showed similar Rho silencing effects but far less retinal transcriptional perturbations compared to ZF6-KRAB.
source: Indeed, ZF6-DB, being exclusively a DNA-binding protein identical to the DBD of ZF6-KRAB, showed similar Rho silencing effects but far less retinal transcriptional perturbations.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data comparing DEGs between ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB.

claim: The specificity is conferred by both the engineered design of the DNA-binding on a genome-specific target and the lack of the ED.
source: This indicates that the specificity is conferred by both the engineered design of the DNA-binding on a genome-specific target (Beerli and Barbas, 2002) and the lack of the ED.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB effects, supported by citation.

claim: ZF6-cis CRE is necessary for Rho expression genome-wide.
source: In addition, this finding supports the notion that that ZF6-cis CRE is necessary for Rho expression genome-wide.
evidence: This is inferred from the deletion and silencing experiments.

claim: AAV8 vector delivery of ZF6-DB resulted in significantly higher functional protection in both the A- and B-wave components of ERG compared to ZF6-KRAB and AAV-GFP controls in RHO-P347S mice.
source: Strikingly, AAV8 vector delivery of ZF6-DB resulted in significantly higher functional protection in both the A- and B-wave components of electroretinography (ERG analysis) compared to ZF6-KRAB and AAV-GFP controls (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by ERG data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Injection of either ZF6-KRAB or ZF6-DB in C57Bl/6 wild type retina did not produce detectable functional detrimental effects.
source: In addition, injection of either ZF6-KRAB or ZF6-DB in C57Bl/6 wild type retina did not produce detectable functional detrimental effects (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is supported by ERG data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The RHO-P347S mouse harbors the P347S RHO human mutant allele including the 20 DNA base pairs of the human genomic ZF6-cis sequence.
source: To test the functional activity of ZF6-DB in an adRP animal model, we used the RHO-P347S mouse (Li et al., 1996), which harbors the P347S RHO human mutant allele including the 20 DNA base pairs of the human genomic ZF6-cis sequence
evidence: This is a description of the animal model used, supported by citation.

claim: The murine Rho promoter sequence lacks the ZF6-Cis target.
source: whereas the murine Rho promoter sequence lacks the ZF6-Cis target (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a) (Li et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a and citation.

claim: Human-specific P347S RHO silencing by ZF6-DB (which does not affect murine Rho expression) may result in preservation of retinal function.
source: Therefore, human-specific P347S RHO silencing by ZF6-DB (which does not affect murine Rho expression) may result in preservation of retinal function (Mussolino et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citation and experimental design.

claim: Administration of the DBR-R vector resulted in rod-specific transcriptional repression of the porcine Rho (38%) and in concomitant replacement of the exogenous hRHO (68%).
source: Administration of the DBR-R vector resulted in rod-specific transcriptional repression of the porcine Rho (38%) and in concomitant replacement of the exogenous hRHO (68%), as assessed by transcripts, protein expression levels, and integrity of photoreceptor outer segments (Figure 4b–d and Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR, Western blot, and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4b-d and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Gnat1 transcript and protein levels demonstrated complementation, supporting a secondary down-regulation of Gnat1 associated with Rho repression.
source: Notably, Gnat1 transcript and protein (data not shown) levels demonstrated complementation, supporting a secondary down-regulation of Gnat1 associated with Rho repression (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Photoreceptor genomic binding of a 20 bp-long DNA sequence by a synthetic DNA-binding protein dramatically reduces Rho expression.
source: In this study, we showed that photoreceptor genomic binding of a 20 bp-long DNA sequence by a synthetic DNA-binding protein dramatically reduces Rho expression.
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The combination of Rho transcriptional silencing and the restricted transcriptome perturbation induced by ZF6-DB indicate that the local binding to ZF6-cis per se is the determinant of transcriptional repression.
source: The combination of Rho transcriptional silencing and the restricted transcriptome perturbation induced by ZF6-DB, without the intrinsic repression activity contained in an ED, indicate that the local binding to ZF6-cis per se is the determinant of transcriptional repression
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The high specificity observed may result by both DNA-binding specificity (biochemical affinity) of ZF6-DB and the rod genomic context.
source: whereas the high specificity observed may result by both DNA-binding specificity (biochemical affinity) of ZF6-DB and the rod genomic context.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The transcriptional repression mechanism of ZF6-DB binding likely relies on the interference occurring between TFs and local DNA sequence features within the RHO proximal promoter region.
source: The transcriptional repression mechanism of ZF6-DB binding likely relies on the interference occurring between TFs and local DNA sequence features within the RHO proximal promoter region (Mitton et al., 2000), which we showed here to be necessary to control Rho expression at the genomic level.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis based on the experimental results and citation.

claim: The lack of known TFBSs and the low level of expression of ZF6-DB suggest that the molecular determinant of silencing may not be the simple displacement of key RHO TFs.
source: The lack of known TFBSs and the low level of expression of ZF6-DB expressed in the photoreceptors, which was twenty-fold below the levels of photoreceptor specific TFs (Crx and Nrl), suggest that the molecular determinant of silencing may not be the simple displacement of key RHO TFs (Mao et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental observations and citation.

claim: The molecular features of the DNA (loop, twisting, bending) may contribute to Rhodopsin transcriptional output.
source: We propose a model in which the molecular features of the DNA (loop, twisting, bending, for instance) may contribute to Rhodopsin transcriptional output.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors.

claim: The DNA may be envisaged as not being exclusively the source of storage of functional information or an inert DNA-binding protein harbor, but also as an intrinsically active operator of the transcriptional function.
source: In this context, the DNA may be envisaged as not being exclusively the source of storage of functional information (protein coding and non-coding transcripts) or an inert DNA-binding protein harbor (i.e. positional information for TFs DNA binding), but also as an intrinsically active operator of the transcriptional function.
evidence: This is a conceptual interpretation proposed by the authors.

claim: This contribution of DNA is supported by both the transcriptional repression upon the ZF6-cis deletion of 20 bp of DNA and interference in trans by using a synthetic DNA binding protein.
source: This contribution of DNA is supported by both the transcriptional repression upon the ZF6-cis deletion of 20 bp of DNA and intereference in trans by using a synthetic DNA binding protein that, not being encoded by the genome, may occupy a protein-free portion of the genome.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: A relevant property of ZF6-DB DNA binding interference is the high rate of transcriptional silencing observed after in vivo gene transfer, which is consistent with canonical TFs mode of action.
source: From a therapeutic prospective, a relevant property of ZF6-DB DNA binding interference is the high rate of transcriptional silencing observed after in vivo gene transfer, which is consistent with canonical TFs mode of action (Kiang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results with therapeutic implications, supported by citation.

claim: DNA binding interference via ZF6-DB in transduced retina generated 45% Rho transcriptional repression, which reached 85% when rods were sorted.
source: DNA binding interference via ZF6-DB in transduced retina generated 45% Rho transcriptional repression, which reached 85% when rods were sorted, supporting its use for diseases requiring correction of a large number of affected cells, such as adRP and other Mendelian disorders due to gain-of-function mutations.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results with therapeutic implications.

claim: Rho transcriptional silencing and its complete RHO replacement support in principle the use of the DBR-R constructs for treatment of any RHO mutation including those caused by a dominant negative mechanism.
source: Furthermore, Rho transcriptional silencing and its complete RHO replacement support in principle the use of the DBR-R constructs for treatment of any RHO mutation including those caused by a dominant negative mechanism (Mao et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results with therapeutic implications, supported by citation.

claim: The 38% silencing and replacement observed may not yet be sufficient to achieve therapeutic efficacy/benefit in patients with adRP.
source: However, the 38% silencing and replacement observed may not yet be sufficient to achieve therapeutic efficacy/benefit in patients with adRP.
evidence: This is a cautious interpretation of the therapeutic potential based on the experimental results.

claim: In vivo retinal gene transfer of an AAV vector carrying a 22 kDa orthogonal and gene-extrinsic noise-resistant synthetic protein acts as a transcriptional repressor, which results in a potent and specific silencing of the Rho gene upon binding to an essential Rho DNA element.
source: In conclusion, in vivo retinal gene transfer of an AAV vector (Doria et al., 2013; Liang et al., 2001; Scatchard, 1949) carrying a 22 kDa orthogonal (Surace et al., 2005) and gene-extrinsic noise-resistant (the permissive rod photoreceptor cell-specific environment; [Li et al., 2011]) synthetic protein acts as a transcriptional repressor, which results in a potent and specific silencing of the Rho gene upon binding to an essential Rho DNA element.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: AAV8-hRHO-cis-del-eGFP resulted in decreased transduction (about fifty fold) compared with hRHO.
source: qReal Time PCR of mRNA levels (2^-ΔCT) on the adult porcine retina 15 days after vector delivery of either AAV8-hRHO-eGFP (n=2) or AAV8-hRHO-cis-del-eGFP (n=2) subretinally administered at a dose of 1x1010, showed that AAV8-hRHO-cis-del-eGFP resulted in decreased transduction (about fifty fold) compared with hRHO.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Histology confirmed the decrease of eGFP expression in hRHO-cis-del-eGFP injected retina compared with the retina injected with hRHO-eGFP.
source: Histology confirmed the decrease of eGFP expression in hRHO-cis-del-eGFP injected retina compared with the retina injected with hRHO-eGFP.
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The treatment with ZF6-DB determined collapse of the outer-segment (OS) with apparent retention of nuclei in the outer nuclear layer (ONL).
source: The treatment with ZF6-DB determined collapse of the outer-segment (OS) with apparent retention of nuclei (stained with DAPI) in the outer nuclear layer (ONL).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: White arrows indicate co-localization of both HA-tag-ZF6-DB and Gnat1 rods depleted of Rho, whereas yellow arrows showed residual Rho and Gnat1 positive cells lacking ZF6-DB.
source: White arrows indicate co-localization of both HA-tag-ZF6-DB and Gnat1 rods depleted of Rho, whereas yellow arrows showed residual Rho and Gnat1 positive cells lacking ZF6-DB.
evidence: This is a description of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: eGFP positive sorted cells (AAV8-GNAT1-eGFP) corresponded to 17.3% of the analysed population.
source: eGFP positive sorted cells (AAV8-GNAT1-eGFP) corresponded to 17,3% of the analysed population (left panel; P2 area, green dots)
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: 22.4% of eGFP positive cells in the retina that received both vectors (AAV8-GNAT1-eGFP and AAV8-CMV-ZF6-DB).
source: whereas, 22,4% of eGFP positive cells in the retina that received both vectors (AAV8-GNAT1-eGFP and AAV8-CMV-ZF6-DB; right panel; P2 area, green dots).
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: qPCR ChIP analysis showed RHO-specific enrichment on RHO TSS region in transfected HEK293 cells.
source: qPCR ChIP analysis of RHO TSS region including ZF6-cis site), GNAT1, ARR3 and tubulin beta proximal promoters controls in transfected HEK293 cells (n=3 indipendent expermients). RHO-specific enrichment is shown on RHO TSS region.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Delivery of AAV8-CMV-ZF6-KRAB resulted in up-regulation of 10 genes associated with inflammatory responses and the down-regulation of 7 genes associated with the rod phototransduction cascade.
source: Delivery of AAV8-CMV-ZF6-KRAB resulted in up-regulation of 10 genes associated with inflammatory responses (red, up-regulation) and the down-regulation (green) of 7 genes associated with the rod phototransduction cascade.
evidence: This is supported by pathway analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a.

claim: The ZF6-KRAB apparent dissociation constant (Kd) is 108.00 ± 11.78 nM (R2 = 0.97).
source: The ZF6-KRAB and ZF6-DB apparent dissociation constants (Kd ZF6-KRAB = 108.00 ± 11.78 nM (R2 = 0.97) and Kd ZF6-DB = 41.94 ± 3.45 nM, R2 = 0.96), respectively) were determined.
evidence: This is supported by gel mobility shift assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b.

claim: The ZF6-DB apparent dissociation constant (Kd) is 41.94 ± 3.45 nM (R2 = 0.96).
source: The ZF6-KRAB and ZF6-DB apparent dissociation constants (Kd ZF6-KRAB = 108.00 ± 11.78 nM (R2 = 0.97) and Kd ZF6-DB = 41.94 ± 3.45 nM, R2 = 0.96), respectively) were determined.
evidence: This is supported by gel mobility shift assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Retinal responses in both scotopic (dim light) and photopic (bright light) showed that both A- and B-waves amplitudes, evoked by increasing light intensities, were preserved in both AAV8-CMV-ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB compared to eGFP control in P347S mice.
source: Retinal responses in both scotopic (dim light) and photopic (bright light) showed that both A- and B-waves amplitudes, evoked by increasing light intensities, were preserved in both AAV8-CMV-ZF6-DB and ZF6-KRAB compared to eGFP control
evidence: This is supported by ERG data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: No functional impairment is observed for each construct (ZF6-DB, ZF6-KRAB, eGFP) in C57Bl/6 mice.
source: A- and B-wave are shown for injected C57Bl/6 mice with ZF6-DB (n=4), ZF6-KRAB (n=4) and eGFP (n=4), independently. No functional impairment is observed for each construct.
evidence: This is supported by ERG data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: AAV8-hRHO-s-ΔZF6-eGFP resulted in decreased transduction (about ten fold) compared with hRHO long.
source: qReal Time PCR, mRNA levels (2^-ΔCT) on the adult murine retina 15 days after vector delivery of either AAV8-hRHO short-eGFP or AAV8-hRHO-s-ΔZF6-eGFP subretinally administered at a dose of 1x109, showed that AAV8-hRHO-s-ΔZF6-eGFP resulted in decreased transduction (about ten fold) compared with hRHO long.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2a.

claim: Histology demonstrated maintenance of rod-specific expression by AAV8-RHOΔ-eGFP.
source: Histology demonstrated maintenance of rod-specific expression by AAV8-RHOΔ-eGFP.

claim: Immunofluorescence double staining showed rod specific transduction of DBR-R (AAV8-RHOΔ-ZF6-DB-GNAT1-hRHO) 2 months after vector delivery.
